humanities_role_explanation: People biographies (sampled from Wikidata/Wikipedia) supply the generation prompts, but the competence tested is general factual precision of long-form generation, not disciplinary humanities competence.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Text-only: prompts 'Tell me a bio of <entity>' and LM-generated biographies, decomposed into atomic facts and checked against English Wikipedia text.
analytical_tasks_explanation: LMs generate biographies (long-form generation); each atomic fact is labeled Supported/Not-supported/Irrelevant against Wikipedia (fact verification of 'atomic facts'). Breaking generations into atomic facts is a form of information extraction. Correct generation relies on factual recall of entity knowledge, including rare entities.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Scoped to a single task: factual precision of people biographies against Wikipedia.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: InstructGPT, ChatGPT, PerplexityAI (human eval); plus GPT-4, Alpaca, Vicuna, Dolly, Oasst-pythia, StableLM-tuned, MPT Chat via the automated estimator.

quantitative_metrics.note: FActScore (% atomic facts supported), Error Rate vs human FActScore, ranking consistency, F1 micro, Pearson r.

summary: The paper introduces FActScore, which decomposes long-form generations into atomic facts and computes the share supported by a knowledge source (Wikipedia). It reports human-annotated FActScores for three commercial LMs and presents an automatic retrieval+LM estimator with <2% error, used to evaluate 13 subjects on 500 biographies each.
key_findings: Human FActScores: InstructGPT 42.5, ChatGPT 58.3, PerplexityAI 71.5. Scores drop for rarer entities (ChatGPT 80% to 16%) and for later positions in generations. Estimator error rate under 2% (best variants), retrieval helps substantially. GPT-4 and ChatGPT are more factual than public models; all LMs less factual than humans; Vicuna and Alpaca are best public models.
dataset_size: 183 human-annotated people entities (549 annotated generations) plus 500 unlabeled entities for 13 subjects (6,500 generations)
evaluation_unit: people entity (biography generation prompt), each decomposed into atomic facts
facets_explanation: Freelance fact-checking experts hired via Upwork revised InstructGPT-generated atomic facts and labeled each as Supported/Not-supported/Irrelevant against English Wikipedia; 10% of data was double-annotated (96/90/88% agreement). Each fact has a single binary label; the paper treats disagreement as limitation cases (70% attributed to debatability, mistakes) and assumes support is 'undebatable'. Answering requires parametric knowledge of the person, which is not in the prompt.
results_explanation: Table 1 'FACTSCORE 42.5 58.3 71.5' for InstructGPT, ChatGPT, PerplexityAI (human evaluation); the headline is PerplexityAI 71.5 on FActScore (percentage of supported atomic facts, not a standard metric, so labeled 'other'). Format gap: estimator variants with and without retrieval differ (e.g. ChatGPT No-context ER 39.6 vs Retrieve→LM 5.1 for InstructGPT), but no single points figure is extracted. Human baseline: human-written bios are scored by the estimator and exceed all LMs, but no exact number is given in text, so human_gap_points is null.

humanities_role.quote: We evaluate FACTSCORE on the task of generating people biographies because generations consist of verifiable statements rather than debatable or subjective ones

dataset_size.quote: In total, we evaluate 6,500 generations from 13 subjects, which would have cost $26K if they were evaluated by humans.
We sample 183 people entities from Wikidata who have corresponding Wikipedia pages.

evaluation_set_size.quote: We sample 183 people entities from Wikidata who have corresponding Wikipedia pages.

primary_evaluation_setting.quote: The validation is based on zero-shot prompting of an LM referred to as an LMEVAL

gold_source.quote: We recruit fact-checking experts—freelancers who mentioned fact-checking as their expertise—for Step 3.

gold_beyond_stimulus.quote: We feed a prompt “Tell me a bio of <entity>” to the LMSUBJ and take a generation as it is.

answer_multiplicity.quote: assigning a binary label to each atomic fact, allowing a fine-grained evaluation of factual precision

plurality_treatment.quote: Whether or not an atomic fact is supported by C is undebatable.

human_baseline_reported.quote: All LMs are substantially less factual than humans.
